---
title: "Switching from Chameleon"
---

chameleon-rs runs code written for Chameleon unchanged. There are two ways to switch: install
the compatibility alias and change nothing else, or change your imports.

## One line: `compat.install()`

Add this at the very top of your app's entry point (the module your server imports, or
`__main__`), before anything imports Chameleon:

```python
import chameleon_rs.compat

chameleon_rs.compat.install()
```

From then on:

| Your code imports | It gets |
|---|---|
| `chameleon`, `chameleon.zpt.template`, `chameleon.tales`, ... | the chameleon-rs module of the same name |
| `chameleon_partials` | `chameleon_rs.partials` (built in) |
| `chameleon_flask` (and `.engine`, `.exceptions`) | `chameleon_rs.flask` (built in) |
| `fastapi_chameleon` (and `.engine`, `.exceptions`) | `chameleon_rs.fastapi` (built in) |

```{python}
import chameleon_rs.compat

chameleon_rs.compat.install()

import chameleon
from chameleon import PageTemplate

print(chameleon.__name__)
print(PageTemplate('<p>${1 + 1}</p>')())
```

Stock Chameleon doesn't need to be installed, and chameleon-rs never imports it. Libraries
that use Chameleon internally, such as chameleon-robyn, get
chameleon-rs the same way. Their own test suites pass on it unmodified.

::: {.callout-warning}
## Install before the first import

`install()` must run before any module imports `chameleon`. If a module was already
imported, `install()` replaces it in `sys.modules` and warns with a `RuntimeWarning` that names
it. Objects imported from it earlier (`from chameleon import PageTemplateLoader` at the
top of a module that's already loaded) stay stock Chameleon objects.
:::

### Keep the original chameleon_partials or chameleon-flask

`install(integrations=False)` maps only `chameleon`. `chameleon_partials` and
`chameleon_flask` then import the original packages, which still render through
chameleon-rs's engine. Use it if you depend on behaviour of those packages that the built-ins
don't copy. A `chameleon_partials.render_partial` from the original package, passed into a
template, still renders natively.

## Or change the imports

Every public name is available from `chameleon_rs` directly:

```python
# Before
from chameleon import PageTemplate, PageTemplateFile, PageTemplateLoader
import chameleon_partials
import chameleon_flask

# After
from chameleon_rs import PageTemplate, PageTemplateFile, PageTemplateLoader
import chameleon_rs.partials as chameleon_partials
import chameleon_rs.flask as chameleon_flask
```

The submodules mirror Chameleon's (`chameleon_rs.zpt.template`, `chameleon_rs.tales`,
`chameleon_rs.utils`, `chameleon_rs.exc`, ...). Chameleon's code-generation internals
(`chameleon.nodes`, `chameleon.program`, `chameleon.zpt.program`, `chameleon.benchmark`)
have no counterpart, since chameleon-rs doesn't generate Python code. Importing them raises
`ModuleNotFoundError`.

After switching, you can simplify: `render_partial` is in every template already, so
`extend_model()` calls and Pyramid `BeforeRender` subscribers that add it can go, and one
`chameleon_rs.configure()` call replaces `register_extensions()` plus `global_init()`. See
[Migrating from the helper libraries](migrating.qmd).

## Check your own app first: shadow mode

Before you switch a production app, you can run both engines side by side on real traffic.
Shadow mode keeps stock Chameleon serving and repeats a sample of renders with chameleon-rs,
then reports any difference in the output or in the exception raised:

```python
import chameleon_rs.shadow

chameleon_rs.shadow.install(sample_rate=0.05)   # serve Chameleon's output, check chameleon-rs's
# chameleon_rs.shadow.install(serve='rust')     # serve chameleon-rs's, check against Chameleon's
```

Differences are logged as warnings on the `chameleon_rs.shadow` logger, with a short diff.
Pass `report=` to handle each `ShadowDifference` yourself.

Shadow mode needs stock Chameleon installed, so don't combine it with `compat.install()`.
Keep in mind:

- Each sampled render happens twice, in the same thread, so its latency doubles. On a
  single-threaded asyncio server, both renders block the event loop. Keep `sample_rate` well
  below 1 (0.01 to 0.1).
- The model is used twice: an iterator argument is used up by the first render, and callables
  run twice. Shadow only side-effect-free renders.
- Templates compiled before `install()` aren't shadowed.

To stop, call `chameleon_rs.shadow.uninstall()`.
